display.purpose: Page-level h1; used sparingly, several pages omit it in favor of the persistent nav's brand name.

title.purpose: Sub-section headings (h3), e.g. paired analytics tables.

body.purpose: Prose, labels, and non-data table cells.

label.purpose: Slug chips and every data-like table column (slug, destination, timestamps).

caption.purpose: Compact functional text that isn't data and isn't prose — the links table's tightened action-button group, and the slug-kind/lock badges next to a slug chip.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Default submit/action button — Signal Blue fill, darkens on hover. Text/fill now clears 4.5:1 AA contrast (was ~4.15:1 at the original #2b7fd1). Every button also gets a min-height: 44px touch-target floor (an audit measured 40px), and a sitewide full-opacity :focus-visible outline (see Focus Indicators) replaces the low-opacity default shown below from an earlier snapshot.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--ss-signal-500, #276fb8); color: #fff; padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; border: 0.0625rem solid var(--ss-signal-500, #276fb8); border-radius: 0.25rem; font-weight: 400; min-height: 44px; transition: background 0.2s ease-in-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #1e6bb8; border-color: #1e6bb8; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ss-signal-500, #276fb8); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Outline / Secondary Row Actions
components.description: Row-level actions (View/Copy/Edit outline; Delete additionally secondary) — de-emphasized rather than warning-colored. Font-size now uses the documented caption token (0.75rem) instead of an off-ramp 0.8rem.
components.css: .ds-row-actions { display: flex; gap: 0.5rem; } .ds-btn-outline { background: transparent; color: var(--ss-signal-500, #276fb8); padding: 0.3rem 0.5rem; border: 0.0625rem solid var(--ss-signal-500, #276fb8); border-radius: 0.25rem; font-size: 0.75rem; } .ds-btn-outline.ds-btn-secondary { color: var(--ss-slate-500, #526078); border-color: var(--ss-slate-500, #526078); } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: rgba(39, 111, 184, 0.08); } .ds-btn-outline.ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: rgba(91, 107, 133, 0.08); }

components.name: Slug Chip
components.description: Signature component: monospace pill marking a shortened link — used in the links table and as the link-detail page's h1. Now plain display text (a <span>) everywhere except where it's a genuine navigation link, since clicking it used to fire a real redirect and inflate that link's own click count. Content differs by context: the detail page's h1 shows the full origin/r/slug URL, the links table shows only /r/slug (full URL in a title attribute) since the origin is identical on every row and was the single biggest contributor to the table overflowing its own container even at a realistic desktop width with a small dataset. The table's chip additionally gets white-space:nowrap + text-overflow:ellipsis past a fixed width, defensive against a long custom slug wrapping the pill onto multiple lines -- scoped to just the table, never the detail page's h1 where the complete slug is the point.
components.css: .ds-chip-slug { display: inline-block; font-family: "SFMono-Regular", "JetBrains Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.85em; background: var(--ss-navy-950, #0a1628); color: #fff; padding: 0.15em 0.6em; border-radius: 999px; line-height: 1.6; } a.ds-chip-slug { text-decoration: none; } a.ds-chip-slug:hover { background: var(--ss-navy-800, #14243d); color: var(--ss-signal-500, #276fb8); }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Plain colored text (no pill/background) marking a link or user as active/disabled — color is redundant with the text label, never the sole signal. ok-green was darkened from #1a7f5a to #177251 after an audit measured the active badge at 4.39:1 against the table cell's real background (Pico paints td/th with --pico-background-color, not the white card behind it) -- just under the 4.5:1 AA minimum for the app's single most common status label. #177251 clears 5.2:1 at the same hue.
components.css: .ds-status-badge { font-weight: 600; text-transform: capitalize; } .ds-status-active { color: var(--ss-ok-500, #177251); } .ds-status-disabled { color: var(--ss-danger-500, #b3261e); }

components.name: Slug-Kind / Lock Badges
components.description: Small caption-scale labels next to a slug chip flagging a custom slug or a password-protected link. Neutral slate, not Signal Blue — a resting-fill use of the accent was tried and reverted (it violated the accent's hover-only rule and failed AA contrast). The two are visually identical except for text, distinguished by label alone. Uses --ss-slate-500, a token distinct from --pico-muted-color and no longer sharing its #5b6b85 value -- --ss-slate-500 was darkened to #526078 for contrast headroom before an audit found it cleared AA by only 0.27:1 against the real table-cell background (not the white card) -- darkened to #526078 (5.6:1) for real margin. The 'not yet live' schedule annotation shares this same token and fix.
components.css: .ds-slug-kind-badge, .ds-lock-badge { display: inline-block; margin-left: 0.35em; font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; vertical-align: middle; color: var(--ss-slate-500, #526078); }

components.name: Schedule State Text
components.description: Text-suffixed (never color-only) states appended to a formatted date: "(not yet live)" for a future start_at (neutral slate — informational, not an alarm), "(expiring soon)" for an end_at within 24h, "(expired)" for one already past (both danger-red, distinguished from each other by suffix text alone).
components.css: .ds-not-yet-live { color: var(--ss-slate-500, #526078); font-weight: 600; } .ds-expiring-soon, .ds-expired { color: var(--ss-danger-500, #b3261e); font-weight: 600; }

components.name: Form Success Banner
components.description: The link-creation flow's payoff moment: a flex row holding the new slug chip plus a Copy button, in ok-green, mirroring form-error's weight/spacing. Introduced so a completed action has a visible result instead of the form silently clearing.
components.css: .ds-form-success { display: flex; align-items: center; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.5rem; color: var(--ss-ok-500, #177251); font-weight: 600; margin-top: 0.5rem; }

components.name: Persistent Nav Shell
components.description: The app-shell chrome rendered on every authenticated page: a persistent brand mark + wordmark (always a link to the dashboard, with a small hand-authored link-glyph SVG icon in Signal Blue), an optional breadcrumb page label, an identity chip (initial-avatar badge + name/role stack, replacing plain 'username (role)' text), a conditional 'Manage users' link (hidden on the Manage Users page itself), and logout. Keyboard focus gets a full-opacity Signal Blue outline rather than Pico's default low-opacity ring, which read as nearly imperceptible against the dark-navy fill. Previously the brand was displaced by a generic 'Back to dashboard' link on every page except the dashboard -- a real navigation-confusion bug (the one persistent orientation cue changed per page) fixed by keeping the brand permanent and adding the breadcrumb label alongside it instead. A critique caught .nav-separator/.nav-page-label silently rendering fully opaque white instead of their declared dimmed rgba values -- #app-header nav li's ID-selector color rule (specificity 1,0,2) beat the plain class rules (0,1,0) regardless of source order, the third time this exact specificity shape has bitten this file. Fixed by scoping the selectors to #app-header nav li.nav-page-label etc. The same pass also caught that hiding the breadcrumb below 480px deleted links/detail.html's only page identity on the one viewport that needed it most -- fixed by only hiding the identity chip's role line at that breakpoint, keeping the breadcrumb visible. A subsequent audit found two more gaps: .brand-link and the "Manage users" link measured 38.4px tall, under the 44px touch-target floor the theme already enforces on buttons -- fixed by giving nav <a> elements the same min-height: 44px floor (centered via inline-flex/align-items). It also found .nav-separator's alpha (0.35) measured 3.20:1 against the nav's navy fill, under the 4.5:1 AA text minimum, though the element is aria-hidden and carries no unique information -- alpha raised to 0.5 (5.25:1) for headroom while staying visibly dimmer than .nav-page-label's 0.75.
components.html:

components.css: .ds-nav-shell { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; row-gap: 0.4rem; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; background: var(--ss-navy-950, #0a1628); color: #fff; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; border-radius: 0.25rem; margin-top: 1rem; } .ds-nav-shell ul { display: flex; gap: 1rem; list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; align-items: center; } .ds-nav-shell li, .ds-brand-link strong { white-space: nowrap; } .ds-brand-link { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.45rem; min-height: 44px; text-decoration: none; color: #fff; } .ds-brand-mark { color: var(--ss-signal-500, #276fb8); flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-nav-shell li.ds-nav-separator { color: rgba(255,255,255,0.5); } .ds-nav-shell li.ds-nav-page-label { color: rgba(255,255,255,0.75); font-weight: 600; } .ds-identity-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; } .ds-identity-avatar { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 1.75rem; height: 1.75rem; border-radius: 0.25rem; background: var(--ss-signal-500, #276fb8); color: #fff; font-weight: 700; font-size: 0.75rem; line-height: 1; } .ds-identity-text { display: flex; flex-direction: column; line-height: 1.25; } .ds-identity-name { color: #fff; font-weight: 600; } .ds-identity-role { color: rgba(255,255,255,0.6); font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; text-transform: capitalize; } .ds-nav-shell a:hover { color: var(--ss-signal-500, #276fb8); } .ds-nav-shell a:focus-visible, .ds-nav-shell button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ss-signal-500, #276fb8); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 0.25rem; } @media (max-width: 480px) { .ds-identity-role { display: none; } }

components.name: Scrollable Data Table
components.description: Every table lives inside a <figure> with overflow-x: auto. Its own scrollbar is styled (thin, Signal Blue thumb on a border-mist track) rather than left to the OS default, since a default overlay scrollbar (esp. macOS's auto-hiding style) gave no persistent hint that a table scrolls, leaving row actions undiscoverable off-screen. Deliberately a styled scrollbar, not a shadow/gradient edge-fade, to stay inside the No-Shadow Rule. The row-action column (last <td>) is additionally position: sticky; right: 0 with a solid background and a border-mist left border, so actions stay reachable at the visible right edge no matter how far the table has scrolled or how wide other columns (Destination, Permissions) grow. Below 600px, the least-essential columns hide outright (Owner/Destination/Created/Starts on the links table; Permissions on the users table) rather than relying on scroll to reveal them, and the column immediately before the sticky one gets an explicit max-width so wrapped content can never physically reach the sticky column's screen position — a sticky column being reachable doesn't mean nothing is hidden underneath it, since it paints on top of whatever occupies its screen position regardless of that content's own position in the table's normal flow. Only max-width on the column itself works for this; padding-right (alone or combined with text-align:right) was tried and measured to have zero real effect. The max-width cap must include the <th>, not just the <td> (a table sizes a column to its widest cell across every row, header included), and every column before the capped one also needs its own cap -- a single long custom slug anywhere in the table widens the Short-link column for every row, pushing later columns rightward and silently defeating a downstream column's clearance even though that cap's own value never changed. The flex-based mobile fixes (flex-wrap, gap, max-width) also require an actual [role=group] wrapper to apply at all -- one table's plain action buttons were never wrapped in one, so an earlier gap rule targeting [role=group] silently matched nothing and the buttons stacked with zero gap regardless.
components.css: .ds-table-figure { overflow-x: auto; scrollbar-width: thin; scrollbar-color: var(--ss-signal-500, #276fb8) var(--pico-muted-border-color, #d6deea); } .ds-table-figure::-webkit-scrollbar { height: 8px; } .ds-table-figure::-webkit-scrollbar-track { background: var(--pico-muted-border-color, #d6deea); border-radius: 999px; } .ds-table-figure::-webkit-scrollbar-thumb { background-color: var(--ss-signal-500, #276fb8); border-radius: 999px; } .ds-table-figure table thead th:last-child, .ds-table-figure table tbody > tr:not(.edit-row) td:last-child { position: sticky; right: 0; background: var(--pico-card-background-color, #fff); border-left: 1px solid var(--pico-muted-border-color, #d6deea); }

components.name: Confirmation Dialog
components.description: Replaces the native confirm() for destructive actions (link delete, user delete) with Pico's own dialog/article component, built dynamically by a shared confirmDialog(message) helper rather than duplicated markup per page. Dismissible via Cancel, Esc, or a backdrop click. Button styling deliberately inverts the row-level convention: Cancel is Pico's plain default (primary) button, Confirm/Delete stays outline+secondary — the same de-emphasis the row Delete button already uses — so the visually prominent button is the safe one, not the destructive one. Narrowed to 26rem and centered (message + footer both), overriding Pico's own wide, left-message/right-footer dialog default, which read as lopsided for a short one-line message.
components.html: Delete the link "promo-2026"? This can't be undone.
components.css: .ds-confirm-dialog > article { max-width: 26rem; text-align: center; } .ds-confirm-dialog > article > footer { text-align: center; } .ds-btn-outline.ds-btn-secondary { color: var(--ss-slate-500, #526078); border-color: var(--ss-slate-500, #526078); background: transparent; }

components.name: Progressive Disclosure (Details)
components.description: Occasional-use fields for a primary "paste and submit" action collapse behind a native <details>/<summary> — Pico's own styled accordion (chevron marker, color-shift summary), not a bespoke JS show/hide toggle. The link-creation form is the current example: Destination URL renders unconditionally since it's the one field every submission needs, while custom slug, schedule (Starts/Expires), and password protection collapse behind a "More options" summary, closed by default and reset to closed after each successful create.
components.css: /* Pico styles <details>/<summary> natively — no custom CSS required. */

components.name: Focus Indicators
components.description: A full-opacity 2px solid signal-blue outline, sitewide, on every focusable element. Pico's own default focus ring is a low-opacity rgba box-shadow that measures ~1.71:1 against a white card -- well under WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 non-text-contrast minimum -- and was originally fixed for the persistent nav alone (its dark-navy fill made the default ring nearly invisible). An audit later found the identical unfixed problem on every other focusable element sitewide, generalized to one sitewide :focus-visible rule. Pico's own higher-specificity `details summary:focus-visible:not([role])` rule (used by the create-link form's "More options" toggle) silently wins over a plain :focus-visible override -- confirmed live -- so a matching-selector-shape override was added specifically for it, relying on load order to break the equal-specificity tie. Re-verified by a 3rd audit pass: every focusable element, including the create-link form's "More options" summary, correctly shows the full-opacity outline -- this fix is holding.
components.css: :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ss-signal-500, #276fb8); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: var(--pico-border-radius); } details summary:focus-visible:not([role]) { outline: 2px solid var(--ss-signal-500, #276fb8); outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview: A quiet, dark-navy control room where every accent-blue "signal" marks a link actively routing traffic. The system already names its own accent `signal-500` in code — the metaphor isn't imposed, it's read off what's there. This is an internal operations console for a marketing team creating and tracking campaign links, not a marketing surface itself: density and scanability outrank expression, and the one confirmed brand instruction so far is "dark theme preferred" over any specific identity. Nothing here is officially locked — treat the palette and component choices below as the incumbent system to preserve during refinement, not an untouchable brand.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-navy chrome (persistent nav, slug chips) against a light, cool-gray content surface — dark accents on a light working canvas, not a fully dark UI
Flat and bordered, never shadowed — depth comes from a border-mist hairline and background contrast, not elevation
Monospace reserved strictly for data (slugs, URLs, timestamps), never as decoration
A pinned, non-scaling type/spacing scale — deliberately rejects Pico's default prose-scaling behavior in favor of admin density

rules.name: The Chrome-Equals-Heading Rule
rules.body: Deep Navy (#0a1628) is the single dark value used for both the nav bar's fill and every heading's text. There is no separate "chrome color" — the darkest neutral just gets reused for both jobs.

rules.name: The Data-Is-Mono Rule
rules.body: Monospace is used for exactly one purpose: columns and chips that carry a slug, URL, or timestamp. It never appears as a "technical-looking" costume elsewhere.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Nothing in this system casts a shadow. Separation between surfaces is border + background-contrast only.

rules.name: The Pill-Is-For-Links Rule
rules.body: Full pill rounding (999px) is reserved for the slug chip — the product's signature "this is a shortened link" marker. No other component uses it.

dos: Do keep --pico-font-size pinned at 100% — this app rejects Pico's default viewport-scaling type, deliberately, because it's a dense admin tool.
Do reserve the 999px pill radius for the slug chip only.
Do reserve the monospace font for slug/URL/timestamp data, never as a "technical" decorative costume.
Do route every form/page error through .form-error rather than a one-off inline style.
Do give a real completed action visible payoff (see .form-success) instead of a silent form-clear — apply this to every flow that completes an action, not just the one that first motivated the rule.

Do style scrollable tables' own scrollbar (thin, Signal Blue thumb on a border-mist track) rather than relying on the OS default, since an auto-hiding overlay scrollbar gives no persistent hint that a table scrolls.

Do use confirmDialog() (app.js) for destructive-action confirmation instead of the native confirm() — and keep Cancel as the visually prominent button, Confirm/Delete de-emphasized, matching the row-level Delete convention.

Do keep a table's row-action column reachable via a sticky column (position: sticky; right: 0, solid background, hairline border) rather than letting actions scroll out of reach or capping other columns' content to force a fit.

Do collapse occasional-use fields behind a native <details> disclosure when a form's primary action centers on one common field — matches the platform's own accordion idiom instead of a bespoke toggle.

Do explicitly set --pico-card-box-shadow (and --pico-dropdown-box-shadow) to none in theme.css — Pico's defaults resolve to a real multi-layer shadow, and overriding every other --pico-card-* property except this one meant every card silently violated the No-Shadow Rule for the theme's entire history.

Do cap a column's own max-width (not padding-right, and not padding-right + text-align:right) to keep its content clear of a sticky neighbor column — padding-right doesn't move left-aligned content, and combined with text-align:right the padding terms cancel out once the cell's own width is also padding-driven in an auto-layout table.

Do set color-scheme: light and explicitly override --pico-form-element-background-color/-border-color/-color/-placeholder-color -- without this, every text input silently inherits Pico's separate prefers-color-scheme: dark form-element palette on any OS/browser set to prefer dark colors, with no in-app opt-out, since data-theme is never set anywhere.

Do use a sitewide :focus-visible rule with a full-opacity outline color, and check for higher-specificity element-specific default rules (e.g. Pico's details summary:focus-visible:not([role])) that can silently win over a generic override -- match the specific selector's shape rather than assuming a lower-specificity generic rule reaches everywhere.

Do cap every column before a clearance-capped column too, not just the one immediately adjacent to a sticky neighbor -- an HTML table shares column width across every row, so a long value anywhere in an earlier column can push a later column's position rightward and silently defeat its own unchanged cap.

Do verify a [role=group] wrapper actually exists before relying on flex-based CSS (flex-wrap, gap, max-width) to apply to a button group -- a rule that looks correct can silently match nothing if the markup never wraps the buttons in one.

Do add a min-height: 44px floor to every button/[role=button] rather than restoring the tightened --pico-form-element-spacing-vertical toward Pico's default -- that variable also drives text-input tap targets, so loosening it to fix button height would undo the deliberate admin-density type scale.

Do keep the persistent nav's brand mark permanent and clickable on every authenticated page -- never displace it with a page-specific 'back' link, which makes the one thing a user orients by change depending on which page they're on. Identify a sub-page via a breadcrumb label next to the brand instead.

Do hide a nav link to the page currently being viewed rather than showing it as a self-referential link to itself -- confirmed as a real navigation-confusion source (a 'Manage users' link visible while already viewing the Manage Users page).

Do extend the sitewide 44px min-height floor to plain nav <a> elements (brand mark, text links), not just button/[role=button] -- an audit found the persistent nav's own brand-link measured 38.4px, since the button-family rule never covered plain anchors even in the one component that should exemplify the standard.
donts: Don't add a box-shadow anywhere — the system is flat by construction, not by oversight.
Don't introduce a second error/status red — danger-red (#b3261e) is now the one value used by both status badges and form errors.
Don't let a page-level heading imply every page needs one — several pages intentionally rely on the persistent nav's brand name instead of a redundant h1.
Don't add a shadow/gradient edge-fade to signal a scrollable region — that would violate the No-Shadow Rule; use a styled scrollbar instead.

Don't assume color-scheme: light blocks prefers-color-scheme: dark media queries from matching -- it only hints the browser's native chrome (scrollbars, autofill) toward light rendering. The only real defense against a vendor stylesheet's dark-mode block is overriding every value it sets, unconditionally, outside any media query.

Don't add a new class-only CSS rule inside #app-header nav without checking it against #app-header nav li { color: #fff; } first -- that ID-selector rule (specificity 1,0,2) silently beats any later plain-class rule (0,1,0) targeting the same or a descendant li, regardless of source order. Verify any new nav li-scoped color rule with getComputedStyle before considering it done; this specificity shape has caused 3 silent bugs in this file already.
